results.prefix: Materials play two roles in a chip factory
results.text: Materials play two roles in a chip factory: they become part of the finished device, or they help manufacture it. Some do both. Consumables are the materials used up or regularly replaced during manufacturing. Silicon is the main starting surface, or substrate, for most chips in this course. Other semiconductors can make better power switches, radio components or light sources. Consumables do different jobs: gases supply atoms for a film, acids clean a surface, and polishing mixtures remove material. Some supply atoms that remain in the chip; much of what enters the factory is removed or recycled after doing its job.

results.prefix: Intuition: charge gathers at a boundary.
results.text: Intuition: charge gathers at a boundary. In GaN, the centres of positive and negative charge within the crystal do not quite coincide. This built-in separation is called spontaneous polarization. Aluminium gallium nitride (AlGaN) has a different polarization, and stretching it to fit GaN changes that separation further; this strain effect is piezoelectric polarization. At the boundary, the two arrangements do not cancel, leaving a net positive sheet of charge. It attracts electrons into a layer a few nanometres thick. They can move along the boundary but are confined across its thickness. That is what “two-dimensional electron gas” means: mobile electrons inside a solid, not a pocket of gaseous material. The polarization creates the attraction; it does not create electrons or supply energy like a battery.

results.prefix: Intuition: resistivity is a live ion meter.
results.text: Intuition: resistivity is a live ion meter. Dissolved salts supply ions, atoms or groups of atoms with an electrical charge. Those ions carry current through water, so adding salt lowers its resistivity, the material's resistance to current flow after allowing for the measuring cell's size. Even pure water conducts a little: a tiny fraction of its molecules split into H+ and OH- ions. The target of 18.2 MΩ·cm means the water is close to that pure-water limit, not that every ion has vanished. The unit reads “megohm-centimetres.” This measurement mainly answers “how much ionic contamination is present?” It cannot certify the absence of neutral organic molecules, dissolved silica, bacteria or particles; those need separate measurements.

results.prefix: Insulation between neighboring wires has the opposite electrical job
results.text: Insulation between neighboring wires has the opposite electrical job from the gate insulator. At the gate we want strong coupling so the gate can control the channel; between wires we want weak coupling so changing one signal disturbs its neighbors less and requires less charge. A low-k dielectric reduces that unwanted capacitive coupling compared with a material whose charges respond more strongly to an applied electric field. That can lower delay and switching energy, but very porous low-k films can be mechanically fragile. A material that looks ideal in an electrical model must survive etching, cleaning, polishing, assembly and years of temperature changes.
